key_insight: Self-powered microsystems will likely depend on hybrid energy harvesting plus ultra-low-power power management, not on any single transducer or battery replacement alone.
engineering_relevance: For IoT and wearable platforms, the main design challenge is co-optimizing harvester materials, rectification/cold-start PMICs, and storage so the system works reliably in real environments.
method: Surveyed triboelectric, piezoelectric/pyroelectric, indoor PV, RF rectennas, and hybrid harvesters
Compared recent material and device advances such as wear-free TENGs, broadband piezoelectric oscillators, and metamaterial RF harvesters
Critically assessed system-level integration issues including impedance matching, cold-start thresholds, and storage degradation
evidence_signal: The abstract cites specific reported gains such as over 300% broader bandwidth for nonlinear piezoelectric oscillators and multiband/broadband RF harvesting enabled by metamaterial designs.
watch_item: Performance gains in lab prototypes may not translate directly to long-term field operation because storage elements and PMICs can still fail under realistic conditions.
paper_title: Energy Harvesting for Self-Powered Microsystems: A Critical Review of Materials, Power Management, and System Integration
